findings.title: Optimized paginator cannot key datetime audit logs
findings.body: When optimized_pagination=true, OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint paginates AuditLogEntry with OptimizedCursorPaginator and order_by="-datetime". That paginator's get_item_key (paginator.py) does math.floor/ceil on the order-by attribute and value_from_cursor returns the raw numeric cursor. DateTimePaginator exists specifically because datetime values are not numbers: after the first page returns rows, build_cursor calls get_item_key on a datetime and raises TypeError, so the new path 500s whenever the queryset is non-empty. A follow-up request with a numeric cursor would also emit SQL comparing the datetime column to an integer instead of DateTimePaginator's timestamp conversion, so pages would be wrong even if the TypeError were avoided. Keep DateTimePaginator, or implement the same datetime key encoding before using this class on audit logs.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets break or silently rewrite pagination
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result now does start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset and slices the queryset with that start. This runs for every Paginator and DateTimePaginator, not only the new audit-log path. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing (ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported) and PostgreSQL rejects a negative OFFSET, so a previous-page cursor whose offset is negative becomes a 500. Cursor.from_string already accepts a negative middle field (for example "1:-5:1"), so clients can trigger that. For a forward cursor, a negative offset is clamped to 0 and the first page is returned instead of rejecting the cursor, which changes results for every existing cursor-paginated endpoint. The same slice is repeated in OptimizedCursorPaginator when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0 (around line 880); the comments claiming the ORM handles negative slices and that this reaches data "beyond normal pagination bounds" are incorrect. Reject offset < 0 with BadPaginationError, as OffsetPaginator already does, and do not change BasePaginator slicing.

findings.title: No tests for optimized pagination or negative offsets
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator and the organization audit-log branch that selects it (including enable_advanced_features and cursors with a negative offset) are added with no tests. The first successful page of audit logs would have shown the datetime TypeError, and a cursor such as "0:-1:0" would have shown the queryset slice failure and the global BasePaginator clamp. Without those cases, the broken path can ship while the default DateTimePaginator tests still pass.
